knowledge_point.title: Identifying the Local Area Scale Factor of a Transformation

question.:question/problem:
Consider a small rectangle $Δ$ whose bottom-left corner is located at the point $(-3,3)$ with sides parallel to the coordinate axes in the $uv$-plane and whose area is $\delta A.$ Which of the following gives the best approximation for the area of the image of this rectangle under the action of the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}u + v^{2}\\\sin{\left(u + v \right)}\end{bmatrix}?
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the absolute value of the Jacobian determinant gives the local area scale factor of the transformation at that point:

$$
\text{Area}(T(Δ))\approx\left|\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right|\cdot\underbrace{\text{Area}(Δ)}_{\delta A}
$$

Computing the corresponding Jacobian determinant, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}\\& =\begin{vmatrix}1&2 v\\\cos{\left(u + v \right)}&\cos{\left(u + v \right)}\end{vmatrix}\\& =(1)\cdot (\cos{\left(u + v \right)})-(2 v)\cdot (\cos{\left(u + v \right)})\\& =(1-2v)\cos(u+v)\\\left.\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}\right|_{(-3,3)} & =\left(- \left(2 v - 1\right) \cos{\left(u + v \right)}\right)\big|_{u=-3,v=3}\\& =- \left(2 (3) - 1\right) \cos{\left((-3) + (3) \right)}\\& =-5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(Δ)) & \approx|-5|\cdot\delta A\\ & =5\,\delta A.\end{aligned}
$$
